original_title: Countdown: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Dungeon Crawl #2 - A Sophomore Slump?
summary_en: With the Nintendo Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the horizon, we're revisiting key dungeons that made the original a masterpiece.
ai_analysis: Fans eagerly anticipating the Ocarina of Time remake can look forward to experiencing iconic dungeons with a fresh coat of paint.

en.title: 5 Dungeons in Ocarina of Time Remake We Can't Wait to Revisit
en.summary: With the Nintendo Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the horizon, we're revisiting key dungeons that made the original a masterpiece.
en.body:
## 1. Inside the Great Deku Tree
This was our very first taste of Hyrule in 1998, and it remains one of the most memorable introductions to any game. Its gentle learning curve, introducing core mechanics like Link's swordplay and bomb usage, makes it a perfect starting point for new players and a nostalgic return for veterans. The visual redesign for the Switch 2 promises to make the Great Deku Tree's inner workings even more breathtaking.

## 2. Dodongo's Cavern
Emerging from the shadow of the Great Deku Tree, Dodongo's Cavern ramps up the challenge and introduces players to the strategic use of bombs to solve environmental puzzles. The sheer scale of the cavern, filled with rolling boulders and fire-breathing Dodongos, was awe-inspiring back in the day. We're excited to see how the remake handles the iconic Goron dance sequence and the boss battle against Big Dodongo.

## 3. Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly
This dungeon is a unique and frankly bizarre experience, requiring players to navigate the insides of a colossal Zora. The mission to rescue Princess Ruto adds a narrative urgency, and the puzzle-solving involving manipulating the giant's internal organs felt truly innovative for its time. The Switch 2's graphical power should make the slimy, pulsating corridors of Jabu-Jabu's Belly a truly immersive, albeit unsettling, adventure.

## 4. Forest Temple
Stepping into the Forest Temple as adult Link marks a significant shift in tone and complexity. Its ethereal atmosphere, challenging puzzles involving invisible platforms, and the introduction of the Fairy Bow made it a standout. The Sheikah technology hinted at in the original designs could be fully realized in the remake, adding layers to its already intricate design and the memorable Phantom Ganon boss fight.

## 5. Spirit Temple
As the final dungeon before confronting Ganondorf, the Spirit Temple offers a mind-bending experience with its time-traveling mechanics. Players must switch between young and adult Link to solve puzzles and progress, a concept that was revolutionary. The dual nature of the temple, split between light and shadow, provided a visually striking contrast that we're eager to see enhanced with modern graphics and gameplay refinements for its 2026 release.
Bottom Line:Bottom Line: Ocarina of Time's dungeons are timeless, and the Switch 2 remake is set to reignite our passion for them.

content_raw: Cavern club. We are one week closer to the 5th November launch of Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, so that means it's time for my second replay catch-up. For those who missed my adventures Inside the Great Deku Tree last week, I'm replaying the original OoT, one dungeon each week, in the run-up to launch. This time, it's Death Mountain's turn.
